cases.user_text: My new policy has an initial waiting period. Does that mean nothing is covered at all during those first days?

must_include: Answer directly that a waiting period is normally scoped to the coverage named by that rule and does not by itself mean the entire policy is unavailable.
legitimate_dependency: Duration, scope and exceptions require the applicable governed policy wording.
must_not_imply: Do not claim all illnesses or accidents are covered during the period, and do not say there is no insurance at all.
acceptable_clarification: Ask which waiting-period clause/product if exact coverage detail is requested.
unnecessary_deferral: The scoped-vs-no-insurance distinction should be answered immediately.

cases.user_text: Then what is the difference between that and a disease-specific waiting period?

must_include: Use 'that' as the previously discussed initial waiting period and explain that initial/general and disease/procedure-specific waits are distinct scopes.
legitimate_dependency: Exact disease lists, durations and exceptions are product-specific.
must_not_imply: Do not invent a universal duration or disease list.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the product only if exact policy details are requested.
unnecessary_deferral: Do not ask the customer to repeat which waiting period they meant.

cases.user_text: Can more than one of these apply to the same treatment?

must_include: Explain that multiple waiting-period rules can potentially be relevant to the same treatment depending on the policy structure.
legitimate_dependency: Interaction or precedence among waits is product-specific and may depend on customer history.
must_not_imply: Do not invent a rule for which waiting period always wins.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the product/treatment if exact interaction is requested.
unnecessary_deferral: Give the general possibility without deferring entirely.
